# Sticky header and focused controls — 16 October 2026

**DPI-08 / P1:** the Party target-size finding in the earlier inventory reproduces through real interactions. Open Customer c1, activate the directory role tabs through Owner, then Ledger. On a 390px phone the Edit party button is at y=71.5–115.5, under a 113px sticky header. Keyboard focus stays on the partly hidden button; its center hits Global search. Axe reports an effective target height of 11.5px. Enter can open the editor, but the focused/clickable control remains obscured. The explicit baseline regression fails in both themes.

The shared TopBar has different heights when mobile controls wrap and when the viewport/font/language changes. Hardcoded page offsets are brittle. Its existing shared component now measures its own header using ResizeObserver and sets document scroll-padding-top to that height plus 8px. Native focus and scrollIntoView then leave controls below it. Cleanup disconnects the observer and restores the previous inline setting when leaving ERP. No input event, navigation, source data, transaction calculation or visual header layout changes. Dialogs, drawers, fields, carts and tables remain the existing component families.

`PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium node scripts/deep-sticky-focus-browser.cjs` covers eight requested viewport sizes in bilingual mode, plus English and Bangla on phone/desktop, each theme: **24 expected interaction journeys and focused target-size scans**. Actual results and failures are uploaded by CI. Tests perform the real role/tab chain, focus and hit-test Edit party, run axe, open/cancel the editor with keyboard/focus return, change viewport across the wrapping breakpoint, and leave ERP to prove an existing 5px document scroll-padding value is restored. The test sets that prior value during a real SaaS→ERP transition; an early diagnostic attempted to set it before HTML parsing and did not actually establish the prior DOM state.

This closes the **specific reproduced** Party focus obstruction. It does not certify every focus path, scrolling container, mobile software keyboard, screen reader, or nested overlay in the ERP. Wider action inventory and remaining language/contrast review are documented in the independent deep audit slices #121–#123. Backend readiness remains unverified.
